transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 72 minutes (scheduled 1h15)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Shea (CISO, Perch), Maya Patel (Head InfoSec), Jonas Becker (Cloud Architect), Evelyn Cruz (Procurement)

Summary: quick hands-on workshop to map Perch's security controls and evidence needs to Redwood's artifacts and Trust Center access. Ran through SOC2 report availability, ISO scope/SoA, RBAC and SSO, audit log retention/export, KMS/HSM flow, and options for hosted vs private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Action items captured at end.

Topics: SOC 2 Type II availability, ISO 27001 scope and SoA, Trust Center permissions for auditors, RBAC role mapping, SSO/SAML integration, audit log retention and export, KMS integration and key ownership, data residency and VPC/private deployment pricing

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — super appreciate squeezing this in. We're aiming to walk through how Redwood maps to your SOC2 and ISO needs and then get to specific artefacts you need for audit.
[00:14] Liam (Perch): Yeah thanks, quick note — our auditors are asking for the SOC two type two report and the ISO scope, and we also need to see who in Redwood can grant trust center access to our internal audit team.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): Got it. We'll show what the Trust Center looks like, and the access roles. A quick heads up — the naming in the Trust Center can be a little different than your internal nomenclature, so we'll map roles to your R-B-A-C table.
[00:45] Maya (Perch): When you say R-B-A-C mapping, does Redwood support attribute-based rules or just static roles? We're trying to avoid creating a million roles.
[00:58] Priya: We support role-based access with groups and can ingest attributes from SAML assertions — so you can do group-to-role mapping from your IdP. It's not full ABAC yet, but you can approximate it using attributes in the assertion.
[01:20] Jonas: And on the SSO side, is it SAML only or also OIDC? We have a hybrid IdP setup (Okta + internal).
[01:30] Alex: SAML and OIDC supported. We usually recommend SAML for enterprise SSO as it plays nicer with our provisioning flows today. Some customers use OIDC for service accounts.
[01:42] Liam: Cool. On audit logging — retention's a big ask. We need 3 years of immutable logs and access to raw audit events for internal SIEM ingests. How does that map to Redwood's logs?
[01:56] Priya: We emit audit logs for admin actions, API usage and model calls. Logs can be retained in Redwood for X days by default, but you can push a streaming export to your S3 bucket or a syslog endpoint. For immutability you can route to your archive layer with WORM policies.
[02:17] Maya: What's X? We need a ballpark retention number before we talk with infra.
[02:23] Priya: Default retention in hosted tier is 90 days for detailed traces, aggregated metrics longer. For SOC-level evidence customers typically export to S3 for 3+ years. For dedicated/private we can retain longer on the cluster if that's required, but it's generally more cost-effective to ship to your archival store.
[02:41] Jonas: For the export, do you support batched exports and backfill? We have high-throughput usage and need guaranteed delivery to our SIEM.
[02:52] Priya: Yes we have a log export API with at-least-once delivery semantics and a small SDK. We also support periodic batch snapshots if you want to backfill. Delivery guarantees depend on your endpoint's ack behavior.
[03:06] Liam: And KMS — our policy is that we keep control of master keys in KMS/HSM. Where would Redwood hold keys?
[03:15] Alex: Good question — options are: 1) Redwood-managed keys (convenient), 2) Customer-managed keys via cloud KMS where Redwood stores wrapped data keys, or 3) HSM-backed keys in private deployments where the key never leaves your HSM. For the strictest posture you want customer KMS or on-prem HSM.
[03:36] Maya: So can we do envelope encryption with our K-M-S? We don't want Redwood to have unwrapped keys in hosted mode.
[03:43] Priya: Yes — we support envelope encryption: we encrypt model artifacts and sensitive token stores with a data key wrapped by your K-M-S. In hosted mode you grant Redwood an IAM role with Encrypt/Decrypt permission on a key; in private deployments the key stays in your VPC/HSM.
[03:57] Jonas: There's sometimes confusion about inference logs vs input content. Are customer prompts included in audit logs by default? That's sensitive data for us.
[04:08] Alex: By default we log metadata about requests and size, but full request bodies are configurable and we can redact or not retain prompt text for sensitive workloads. For regulated PII flows we recommend private deployment or strict redaction + customer KMS.
[04:25] Liam: Ok that helps. For ISO 27001 we need the SoA and the scope statement. Do you have a canonical scope doc we can attach to our evidence?
[04:35] Priya: Yes, we maintain an ISO scope statement and a Statement of Applicability. We'll share a sanitized SoA and the certified scope PDF. Note some controls in the SoA reference internal Redwood processes — we'll flag ones that map to your responsibility matrix.
[04:52] Maya: How do we get auditor access for the Trust Center? We need time-limited read-only access for the auditor and exports they can download.
[05:02] Alex: We can create a time-limited auditor role and issue a scoped access token. Alternatively you can download artifacts and share them. For large data sets auditors usually prefer direct S3 access or getting CSV exports.
[05:18] Jonas: Any complications with residency? Our customers in EU require data to stay in eu-west-1. Can Redwood guarantee region pinning?
[05:27] Priya: Yes, for hosted we have region pinning for model data and logs; it's a tenancy configuration at provisioning time. If you need strict residency we recommend Dedicated in eu-west-1 or a Private VPC in your cloud region.
[05:40] Liam: Procurement question — what's the typical lead time to set up a private VPC instance with customer-managed KMS?
[05:48] Alex: Typical lead time is 4–6 weeks after contract signature for a standard private deployment; faster if we reuse existing infra templates. We'll confirm after we see network specs.
[06:00] Evelyn (Procurement): For PO and invoicing we need pricing tiers documented — can you provide a clear sheet for hosted vs dedicated vs private and what SOC2/ISO support level costs extra?
[06:12] Alex: Yes, we'll share a pricing sheet. Security packages like extended log retention and Trust Center retention audit exports are add-ons. We'll itemize them.
[06:22] Maya: For controls mapping — we need to know which Redwood control evidences map to our control IDs. Do you produce a mapping matrix?
[06:31] Priya: We have a controls alignment workbook we can share; it maps Redwood controls to common frameworks and includes sample evidence artifacts. We'll need to customize a mapping for Perch's control IDs — that's what we can produce in the follow-up RBAC/SoA exercise.
[06:48] Jonas: For the log formats: does Redwood use a standard JSON schema for events so we can parse them into our SIEM?
[06:56] Priya: Yes, events are JSON with fields for timestamp, actor, resource, action, request_id, model_id, token_counts. Small variance between runtime versions but we document the schema.
[07:08] Liam: A few quick concerns from our legal team: do you have SOC2 cover for subprocessor management and do you provide a subprocessor list?
[07:17] Alex: We publish a subprocessor list in the Trust Center and disclose third-party subprocessors in the SOC2 report. For more sensitive subprocessors we can provide additional attestation under NDA.
[07:30] Maya: One tricky area — demonstration of access reviews: our auditors asked how often Redwood rotates admin credentials and does access recertification.
[07:40] Priya: Access reviews are quarterly, credentials use MFA and our session manager enforces short token TTLs. We have evidence artifacts for last 12 months of access review cycles which we can include in the SoA pack.
[07:54] Jonas: A quick technical nit — you mentioned KV cache earlier in your docs, I saw a note about KVP cache on the site, can you clarify?
[08:02] Priya: That's our fault, small transcription in docs sometimes says 'KVP' — it's KV cache, stands for key-value cache for model inference. We'll tidy the wording.
[08:12] Liam: Great. Last part — timeline and acceptance criteria. For us success is: 1) auditors have required artifacts and Trust Center access, 2) RBAC mapping completed and validated, 3) log export and retention tested for our SIEM. Can Redwood commit to help run a bench test?
[08:31] Alex: Yes — we'll run a benchmark for log export throughput and a proof-of-export to your S3. We'll also provide the RBAC mapping doc and hold a review session with your InfoSec team.
[08:44] Evelyn: Can we put a tentative week for the benchmarking? We prefer week of Nov 15.
[08:49] Alex: Works for us.
[08:52] Maya: Ok that's all from security side, thank you.
[08:55] Alex: Thanks everyone — quick recap: Alex will upload SOC 2 and ISO artifacts; Priya will deliver RBAC diagram and controls workbook; Jonas to send retention policy; Evelyn to confirm procurement timeline. We'll schedule the benchmark week of 11/15.
[09:10] Liam: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcription quality: speaker overlaps and a couple of product names mis-typed (KVP vs KV) in the auto-generated notes; timestamps approximate. References shared: link to Trust Center (link redacted), sample SoA, controls alignment workbook (to be attached).
